checked.found: Opened 11 November 1215 under Innocent III; Britannica: 400+ bishops, sanctioned transubstantiation, obliged yearly confession.
Hermit elected 5 July 1294 after a roughly two-year vacancy; resigned 13 December 1294, the first pope to abdicate.
Martin V elected 11 November 1417; the council ended the schism by deposing or accepting resignation of claimants and electing Martin V (Britannica/Wikipedia).

Year 1492 confirmed (conclave 6-11 August 1492; Rodrigo Borja born near Valencia; simony widely alleged but unproven, 'reputedly' is apt). The description calls him a 'Renaissance pope', a period word that hints at the era.
checked.suggestion: A Spanish cardinal reputedly bought his way to the papal throne and went on to rule as a notorious pope.

checked.found: Brief Dominus ac Redemptor, 21 July 1773, issued under Bourbon monarch pressure, suppressing the Society of Jesus.
Elected 16 June 1846 as a liberal-leaning choice; reign of nearly 32 years, longest after (uncertain) Peter.
Pastor aeternus promulgated 18 July 1870 by the First Vatican Council, defining papal infallibility.
Ratzinger elected 19 April 2005 in the Sistine Chapel, white smoke, succeeding John Paul II (Polish, long-serving).
Benedict resigned 28 February 2013; Bergoglio of Argentina elected 13 March 2013, first Latin American pope.
Chicago-born Robert Prevost elected 8 May 2025 after Francis died 21 April; first American pope.
